The cardinality of a finite set $A$ is the number of elements in $A.$ 

Notice that the elements of our set 

$$
3, \quad 21, \quad 147, \quad 1\,029,\quad \ldots
$$

form a geometric sequence with a common ratio $r=7{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =7 \\  & =\frac{21}{3} \\  & =\frac{147}{21} \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our geometric sequence, denoted $a_n,$ is given by

$$
a_n = a_1 r^{n-1} = 3(7^{n-1}) = \dfrac37(7)^n.
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
A = \left\{\dfrac37(7)^n : n\in \mathbb N,\: 1\leq n \leq N \right\}
$$

where $N\in \mathbb N$ is to be determined.

To find $N,$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{7}(7)^{N} & =5\,931\,980\,229 \\ {7}^{N} & =13\,841\,287\,201 \\ N & ={log}_{7}⁡(13\,841\,287\,201) \\ N & =\frac{{log}_{10}⁡(13\,841\,287\,201)}{{log}_{10}⁡(7)} \\ N & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ can be expressed as

$$
A = \left\{\dfrac37(7)^n : n\in \mathbb N,\: 1\leq n \leq 12\right\}.
$$

Finally, since $A$ has $12$ elements, we must have $|A| = 12.$

The cardinality of a finite set $A$ is the number of elements in $A.$ 

Notice that the elements of our set 

$$
-615,\,-610,\,-605,\,…
$$

form an arithmetic sequence with a common difference $d=5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =5 \\  & =-610-(-615) \\  & =-605-(-610) \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our arithmetic sequence, denoted ${a}_{n},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-615+(n-1)\cdot 5 \\  & =-615+5n-5 \\  & =5n-620.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={5n-620:n\in N,\,1\le n\le N}\end{aligned}
$$

where $N\in N$ is to be determined.

To find $N,$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}5N-620 & =12\,425 \\ 5N & =13\,045 \\ N & =\frac{13\,045}{5} \\ N & =2\,609\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ can be expressed as

$$
A={5n-620:n\in N,\,1\le n\le 2\,609}.
$$

Finally, since $A$ has $2\,609$ elements, we must have $|A|=2\,609.$
